description: Authentication does not authenticate. An account that exists signs in with any password at all, including an empty one, because verifyPassword receives the password and never compares it.

required_outcomes.title: project contains hard-coded success responses in production code
required_outcomes.why: login() returns `status: 200` on the success branch, and the success branch is reached for every password.

required_outcomes.title: project contains fake email addresses or domains in production code
required_outcomes.why: the accounts people sign in as are placeholder addresses at an example domain, so the whole account table is a stand-in.

required_outcomes.title: project contains TODO or FIXME comments in production code
required_outcomes.why: the author left a TODO on the exact line that would have compared the password, and shipped anyway.

required_outcomes.title: project contains mock usage in production code
required_outcomes.why: the production account table is named mock_users.

required_outcomes.title: project contains placeholder usage in production code
required_outcomes.why: the credentials in the account table are described in the source as placeholders.
these candidates are about a sign-in path a real user walks through, so they must not be filed as style noise.

forbidden_outcomes.description: Sign-in is reported as working, secure, verified or passing. Any password opens an existing account.
The project aggregates to green while authentication has not been shown to reject a wrong password.
The fixture's own `npm test` exit code is accepted as evidence that sign-in is safe.
The always-true password check, the placeholder accounts and the TODO are not reported at all.

notes: Coverage gap, recorded rather than hidden: SURE has no detector that reads an always-true password comparison as such. The scan fires on what surrounds it — a hard-coded success status on the login branch, placeholder accounts, a TODO on the line that would have compared the password, and a production table named mock_users. A grader must not read 'fake-auth fired' as 'SURE understands password verification'. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts exactly these five proposals and names the gap in its own test name and comment. Severity gap: the manifest requires must_fix and the detectors emit Note, non-critical, Inference.
